text:
marco: heads up, noticed recurring 300-500ms tail spikes on the KV cache path for very long contexts (~10-14k tokens) starting after the batching heuristic tweak last night :eyes:
ben: timeline? is this across all pods or one host?
marco: mostly on a subset of pods in us-west-2 ded pool. p50 unchanged, p95 ~120ms -> p95 ~180ms, p99 jumps to 420ms during bursts.
Priya: any steady repro? can we replicate on staging? :thinking:
marco: yep, small stress harness reproduces it within ~2k requests if long-contexts are common and requests hit hotset churn. repro command:
```bash
./tools/repro_kv_rotation.sh --long-contexts --qps 250 --duration 10m
```
Output shows repeated pager pulls and reinsert storms: 
```
[kv] pager_fetch: pages=43, pulls/sec=8.9, reclaim_ms=28.3
[kv] reuse_miss: hotset_evictions=312, reinsert_chain=78
[latency] op_ms p99=423
```
alice: config? FIFO/LRU? recent change was the batching tweak but not eviction.
marco: running FIFO in prod for these pools (we'd flipped to FIFO when we saw LRU lock contention in earlier stress tests). config excerpt:
```yaml
kv_policy: fifo
kv_hotset_ratio: 0.07
kv_probation_ms: 10
kv_pager_batch_limit: 64
```
ben: fifo was meant to be simpler under throughput, but I wonder if FIFO + frequent reinserts under long contexts causes pathological reordering and pages bounced repeatedly. could be correctness/ordering issue rather than pure policy perf.
Priya: I profiled one pod with per-thread stacks + perf: heavy time spent in pager lock and in the reinsert path. stack traces showed kernel selection overhead spikes right when pages are pulled (we switch to a different GEMM kernel for longer sequences which increases scheduling jitter).
marco: yes kernel switch + synchronous pager fetch seems to serialize token generation for some requests. batching heuristic changes made more heterogeneous batches which increases chance of kernel switch mid-batch.
alice: can we mitigate quickly with config change? suggestions?
ben: short term: bump kv_hotset_ratio to 0.16 on a canary pool to reduce pager churn, enable probation window to keep recently reinserted keys out of immediate eviction (kv_probation_ms -> 50). That should lower hotset reinsert storms.
Priya: +1. also flip deterministic-evict-ordering flag to true for the canary so we can see if ordering bug contributes. Add extra tracing on reuse path.
marco: I'll run canary in us-west-2 -> pool ded-usw2-hot-2. plan: 20% traffic, 30m trial, compare p99 and pager pulls.
marco: starting canary now.
devops-bot: deploy started: canary/ded-usw2-hot-2 at 2971234589 - kv_hotset_ratio=0.16, kv_probation_ms=50, deterministic_evict=true
Priya: logs after 10m into canary show pager pulls down 3x and p99 back to ~150ms for canary pods. initial sign looks good.
alice: good signal. next step add a unit/regression test around reinsert ordering and a small stress test with mixed kernel selection to ensure we don't regress when batching heuristics change.
ben: long term: consider hybrid policy that uses a small LRU hot ring for recently accessed entries + FIFO cold ring to avoid thrashing under long contexts. keep policy switchable per-pool.
marco: opened issue with traces attached: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RW-8721 - notes: deterministic-evicting revealed a race where reinserts could be starved by concurrent reclaim.
Priya: I'll take the tracing + test work. marco, can you own canary metrics and rollback if p99 creeps?
marco: yes, will monitor dashboards and set automated rollback at p99 > 300ms for 5m.
alice: thanks all, good quick triage. we'll follow up with a short postmortem if canary stabilizes or if we see recurrence. :thumbsup:
